Since Stripe introduced Radar, we've seen our fraud rate drop to literally zero (low-risk business, no physical shipping).
We are seeing customers with previously very low fraud rates now getting more false positives, causing legitimate customer cards to be declined; lack of easy programmatic control is an issue.

We got a couple false positives; the Stripe UI wasn't clear that you couldn't override the 'block' even though the button was there. A quick email to Stripe support got transactions whitelisted within hours.
It used to be $0.02 per screening, jumped to $0.07.

Not just each failed attempt, but every transaction—previously Radar only checked the card on a subscription at first use, now it checks every transaction unless you opt out (and opting out requires disabling both Radar Standard and per-transaction subscription screening).
This is brutal, especially for small transactions. Note each failed attempt is another screening fee. Unfortunately, there is no good competition.
Allow Rules, if not implemented properly, could open a vector for fraud—that's why it's not enabled by default for newer businesses; users must contact support to turn it on manually.
